skill.name: writing-great-skills
skill.description: Reference for writing predictable AI skills through clear invocation, structured information, precise steering, and disciplined pruning.
skill.summary: Write lean, predictable skills with clear triggers, completion criteria, and information hierarchy.

content.value_statement: AI skills can become difficult to invoke, follow, and maintain. This reference provides a clear vocabulary and practical principles for predictable skill design.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to use model-invoked or user-invoked skills.
Guides trigger descriptions using leading words and distinct branches.
Organizes steps and reference material through an information hierarchy.
Shows when to disclose reference material or split a skill.
Provides pruning methods for duplication, stale content, and no-op instructions.
Diagnoses premature completion, sprawl, negation, and weak legwork.
limitations: Provides reference guidance but does not generate or edit skill files automatically.
Does not execute tests or measure skill behavior across model runs.
Requires author judgment when selecting leading words and completion criteria.
Uses specialized terms that may require consulting the included glossary.

use_cases.title: Draft a First Skill
use_cases.description: Structure invocation, steps, references, and completion criteria before writing the final skill.

use_cases.title: Refine an Existing Skill
use_cases.description: Remove duplication, stale guidance, and no-op instructions while preserving required behavior.

use_cases.title: Standardize a Skill Library
use_cases.description: Apply shared vocabulary and review criteria across related skills and reference files.

prompt_templates.title: Choose an Invocation Mode
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my skill purpose: [purpose]. Recommend model invocation or user invocation, and explain the context and cognitive load tradeoff.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner is deciding how users and agents should discover a skill.

prompt_templates.title: Improve a Skill Description
prompt_templates.prompt: Rewrite this skill description: [description]. Front-load its leading word, keep one trigger per branch, and remove identity repeated in the body.
prompt_templates.scenario: An author wants reliable model invocation with minimal context load.

prompt_templates.title: Restructure Skill Information
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this skill body: [skill text]. Separate steps from reference, identify disclosure candidates, and give every step a checkable completion criterion.
prompt_templates.scenario: An experienced author is improving information hierarchy and execution.

prompt_templates.title: Perform a Full Skill Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this skill and glossary: [content]. Evaluate invocation, branches, hierarchy, co-location, completion criteria, leading words, duplication, relevance, no-ops, sediment, and sprawl.
prompt_templates.scenario: A maintainer needs a comprehensive review before publishing a skill.

output_examples.input: Choose invocation for a skill that only runs when a person requests a release checklist.
output_examples.output: Recommendation: user invocation. The person already controls every invocation, so model discovery would add context load without improving reach.

output_examples.input: Review a long skill containing setup instructions, optional deployment guidance, and repeated definitions.
output: Keep setup steps in the main skill and add checkable completion criteria.
Move optional deployment guidance behind a clearly worded context pointer.
Keep each repeated definition in one authoritative location.

output_examples.input: Diagnose why an agent rushes through research before writing.
output_examples.output: The research step has a vague completion criterion and visible later steps. Define an exhaustive evidence target before considering a sequence split.

best_practices: Use one authoritative location for every rule or definition.
Give each ordered step a checkable and appropriately demanding completion criterion.
Keep shared material inline and disclose branch-specific reference through precise context pointers.
anti_patterns: Do not repeat one trigger using several synonymous phrases.
Do not keep stale or behavior-neutral instructions because deletion feels risky.
Do not split skills unless independent invocation or sequence isolation justifies the added load.

faq.question: What is the main goal of this skill?
faq.answer: It helps authors make agent behavior more predictable by improving invocation, structure, steering, and maintenance.

faq.question: Does this skill create files automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides reference guidance that an agent or author can apply while creating or editing skills.

faq.question: When should a skill use model invocation?
faq.answer: Use it when an agent must discover the skill independently or another skill must reach it.

faq.question: When should reference material move to another file?
faq.answer: Move material when only some branches need it and a precise context pointer can retrieve it reliably.

faq.question: How does this skill reduce premature completion?
faq.answer: It recommends sharpening completion criteria first, then separating later steps only when visible steps still cause rushing.

faq.question: Can teams use the glossary as a review standard?
faq.answer: Yes. The glossary defines shared terms for reviewing invocation, hierarchy, steering, pruning, and common failure modes.
